title: Under overload the one register spends 64-96% of its time on network attempts that are refused, so completions fall past the knee and network completion is ~0 above ~1.5x

A saturated network side takes the exchange's only register from local callers: lines numbered above the network callers get no dial tone at all; below them, dial tone 5.7x slower and half the calls BUSY
Waiting callers are served lowest port first because the register is freed on tick_1k (scan 00); under sustained overload blocks 5x-7x get almost no dial tone, at both scales
Recovery after overload takes one dial-tone timeout (3 s scale 8, 15-20 s real): the backlog is flushed only by callers giving up; nothing is latched
A caller who stops after 1 e b of a real code holds the origin register and a trunk until the register's NODIG (10 s real), because the far refusal is not heard before o_last
